node.reason: LTS only (production.md): new projects start on Node 26, the Active LTS line; add the next LTS major once it starts. 26.13.1 is a security release that fixes nine high CVEs in http2 and TLS

next.reason: 16.4.5 (November 3, 2026 security release) fixes seven medium advisories, among them cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning in "use cache" and HttpOnly cookie exposure on Edge routes; 16.4.1 fixed an RCE in "use cache" and one in Image Optimization

watch.note: Next 17 makes Cache Components the framework default (create-next-app already does since 16.4); on each minor, check whether experimental.turbopackRustReactCompiler and @next/playwright became stable

react.reason: Stable ViewTransition, used by the styling rules

typescript.reason: The rules assume TS 7: its defaults (strict on, no baseUrl), and next build type-checks through the tsc CLI since Next 16.3

watch.note: A typescript-eslint release whose typescript peer range includes 7.x (8.73.0 still stops below 6.1; TS 7.1, which adds the programmatic API, is in beta): typescript-eslint and other API-based tools can move to TS 7. Once no stack is on TS 6: replace typescript-lsp and the global typescript-language-server and typescript@6 (plugin.json, settings.json, USAGE.md, tooling/claude-code/stack.md) with an lspServers entry in plugin.json that starts the project's own TS 7 with tsc --lsp --stdio; Claude Code starts the command from PATH, so check that pnpm exec reaches the project's tsc

pnpm.reason: 12.11.0 adds the permissions setting that approves the skills a dependency ships (tooling/claude-code/rules.md); 12.7.0 makes pnpm runtime's Node follow .node-version and .nvmrc; 12.0 to 12.2 treat an explicit minimumReleaseAge as non-strict and silently let younger versions in; pnpm 12 (stable since August 26, 2026) is a Rust rewrite with the same commands, settings and lockfile as 11; unknown keys in pnpm-workspace.yaml now fail

next-themes.reason: Still 0.x: pin the exact version in the project

watch.note: No release since 0.4.6, and React warns about its theme script on client renders since Next.js 16.2 (pacocoursey/next-themes#385): replace it once shadcn's Next.js dark mode guide does, or follow a fix release

react-hook-form.reason: v8 adds React Compiler support but is still in beta

watch.note: React Hook Form 8 stable release: re-evaluate

zod.reason: Earlier versions are affected by known GitHub advisories (worst: high)

next-intl.reason: Earlier versions are affected by GHSA-8f24-v5vv-gm5j (medium, an open redirect; fixed in 4.9.1) and GHSA-4c35-wcg5-mm9h (medium, prototype pollution through translation catalog keys; fixed in 4.9.2)

orval.reason: Earlier versions are affected by known advisories (worst: critical): an OpenAPI document can inject code into the generated client, such as GHSA-v36f-hqj9-q8rr, fixed in 8.40.0, and GHSA-f96w-763g-hg7v, fixed in 8.41.0; Orval publishes most of them only in its repository, so pnpm audit doesn't report them

@faker-js/faker.reason: 10.5.0 fixes GHSA-qxc2-j82w-r537 (high): helpers.fake can be exploited into arbitrary code execution

postgresql.reason: The rules rely on uuidv7, built in since PostgreSQL 18

watch.note: PostgreSQL 19 GA: re-evaluate; once hosted Supabase offers Postgres 18 or later, Next.js projects on Supabase drop their uuidv7 deviation

drizzle-orm.reason: 0.45.2 fixes CVE-2026-39356 in identifier escaping; 1.0 is still a release candidate

watch.note: Drizzle 1.0 stable release: new projects start on 1.0; ORM, Kit and Seed move to one shared version, and drizzle-zod becomes drizzle-orm/zod

better-auth.reason: 1.7.16 fixes 12 advisories (worst: critical GHSA-4wq4-2ppv-q3hg, the Expo plugin's proxy lets an attacker sign in as a user from their email address; GHSA-q747-mqgr-4gh7, high: unverified phone numbers can be claimed), published only in Better Auth's repository, so pnpm audit doesn't report them

@clerk/nextjs.reason: 7.9.26 is the first version on @clerk/backend 3.28.0, which fixes GHSA-wpqf-h9rq-rg73 (medium): OIDC ID tokens accepted as session tokens; published only in Clerk's repository, so pnpm audit doesn't report it. Earlier 7.x versions are also affected by GHSA-vqx2-fgx2-5wq9 (critical, a middleware route protection bypass) and GHSA-w24r-5266-9c3c (high, an authorization bypass)

payload.reason: 3.93.0 "contains vital security updates" (block child read access in queries, pasteURL restrictions on remote URL uploads, escaped values in the Lexical HTML converters), not yet published as advisories; 3.92.0 pins undici 7.30.1 against the high advisories of undici 7.29; earlier versions are affected by known GitHub advisories (worst: critical); 4.0 is still in beta

@tanstack/react-table.reason: v9 is compatible with React Compiler without "use no memo"

@dnd-kit/react.reason: Still 0.x: pin the exact version in the project

vitest.reason: 5.0.5 fixes GHSA-p458-7748-mcp3 (medium) in @vitest/browser and @vitest/ui, which vitest pins to its own version: the dev server served .env files, keys and .git despite server.fs.deny

@vitest/coverage-v8.reason: Same version as vitest, which pins it as an exact peer dependency

@lhci/cli.reason: Still 0.x: pin the exact version in the project. 0.16.0 drops tmp ^0.1.0, which has GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65 (high, path traversal; fixed only in tmp 0.2.6), and binds its fallback server to loopback; CI's pnpm audit --prod doesn't check dev dependencies

sanitize-html.reason: 2.18.2 fixes GHSA-8g6g-w2rq-xcmc and GHSA-2rjc-9xvg-45j7 (medium, XSS) and GHSA-6wrv-5cp6-h3c5 (low); published only in ApostropheCMS's repository, so pnpm audit doesn't report them. Earlier versions are also affected by known GitHub advisories (worst: critical)

oxlint.reason: The shared configs need options.typeAware (1.51.0), options.denyWarnings (1.52.0), per-extension never in import/extensions (1.73.0) and the per-category React Compiler rules, including react/unsupported-syntax (1.79.0)

watch.note: Oxlint 1.92 discovers tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript 7, for type-aware linting, and Vite+ 1.7 already runs on it: when Oxlint's docs make tsrs the type-aware backend, replace oxlint-tsgolint in the stacks' setup.json and here; trustPolicy: no-downgrade rejects the tsrs release Vite+ 1.7 bundles (oxc-project/tsrs#945), so check that its release installs

oxfmt.reason: Still 0.x: the Renovate preset pins the exact version in the project. 0.77.0 is the version create was verified with on every stack (ADR 0001)

watch.note: Oxfmt 1.0 stable release: drop the exact pin

@sentry/nextjs.reason: The rules use v11's dataCollection; 11.9.0 fixes GHSA-fvxq-xq4h-rqgm (medium): with tunnelRoute, the browser's cookies, HttpOnly session cookies included, were forwarded to Sentry; published only in Sentry's repository, so pnpm audit doesn't report it

@opennextjs/cloudflare.reason: 1.20.16 fixes GHSA-5crp-j778-fgmr and GHSA-3grv-rf6r-fj3x (medium, middleware bypass), published only in its repository, and requires the Next.js November 3, 2026 patches
